jobs.title: Analytics Engineering Manager, Data Platform & Governance
jobs.description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

About Analytics at LawnStarter

We're a small, senior analytics team supporting the entire company, product, marketing, operations, and finance all run on the data we serve. The foundation is solid: a centralized Redshift data warehouse where all source data lands, modeled in dbt and orchestrated by Airflow, with Segment feeding event data in. You won't be stitching scattered sources together, the platform exists; your job is to make it trustworthy and keep it that way. We're mid-migration to Lightdash as our single BI platform, replacing Tableau and Metabase.

Here's the honest gap: everyone on the team today is an analyst. Data quality, tracking standards, and platform hygiene get done as side work, squeezed between analyses. Nobody wakes up thinking about them, which is exactly the job we're hiring for.

The Role

You'll be the first person at LawnStarter dedicated to data governance, the owner of whether our data can be trusted, and of the roadmap that makes it more trustworthy every quarter. Trust means the quality and freshness of our source data, pipelines, and reports; the definitions behind our metrics; the standards behind our Segment event tracking; the health of our Lightdash workspace; the data feeding our machine learning models; and the security of the data itself. The roadmap means sitting with product, marketing, ops, and finance to understand what the business needs from data, turning that into priorities for the platform, and sequencing the work, yours and, soon, your team's.

This is a hands-on role, every manager at LawnStarter builds, and this one is no exception. You'll start solo, with the Analytics team around you: building automation, writing checks, fixing what's broken, and putting processes in place that scale past you. Once you've landed, we open a Lead Analytics Engineer role reporting to you, you'll help choose them, and the function grows from there as scope demands.

**What makes this role different:**

* **You're first.** Governance has been everyone's side job, so what exists today is yours to reshape, keep what works, redesign what doesn't, and your standards become the company's standards.
* **You own the roadmap, not a backlog.** Nobody hands you requirements, you discover what the business needs from data and decide what gets built, in what order, and why.
* **Whole-stack ownership.** Source data to pipelines to dashboards and ML models, you own trust across the entire chain, not one slice of it.
* **A live migration to shape.** Lightdash is landing now. You get to set up its permissions, structure, and norms before bad habits form, instead of untangling them later.

What You'll Own

* **The data roadmap -** discovering what product, marketing, ops, and finance need from data, prioritizing it against platform health, and sequencing the investment. You'll present it, defend it, and re-plan it as the business moves.
* **Data quality and freshness -** automated monitoring across source data, pipelines, and reports; catching upstream schema and source changes before they break anything downstream; running incidents to resolution when they happen.
* **Data lineage and impact analysis -** a living map from production source to warehouse model to dashboard, and the process that uses it: when a production change is proposed, its downstream impact on pipelines, metrics, and reports gets assessed before it ships, not discovered after. The end-state is data contracts with engineering, so breaking changes get caught in their workflow, not ours.
* **Lightdash -** administration, workspace structure, permissions, and the rollout itself. Your job is to give the company self-serve autonomy while keeping the workspace tidy enough that people can find and trust what's there. Enablement is part of the deal, people follow standards they've been taught, and so is keeping queries fast and warehouse costs sane.
* **The semantic layer -** we just shipped it for our most critical metrics: one governed definition per metric, in code. You'll extend definition and mapping to the rest and guard the layer against uncontrolled growth as it scales.
* **Event tracking governance -** our governed Segment event catalog: reviewing new events against its standards, keeping it matched to what production actually sends, and evolving the guardrails (naming, property dictionary, drift detection) as tracking grows.
* **AI data readiness -** AI agents query our warehouse every day through Brain, our internal AI toolkit. You'll govern what data AI tools can access and keep the warehouse AI-legible: documented, consistent, and safe for an agent to query and get the right answer.
* **Data security and privacy -** access controls, PII handling and retention under US state privacy laws, and periodic reviews of who, and which AI tools, can see what.
* **The governance system itself -** the documentation, ownership models, and review loops that keep all of the above running without heroics.

Problems to Solve

**Turn business needs into a data roadmap** Every area of the company wants something from data, and today those asks reach the Analytics team as a stream of interruptions. You'll build the intake and prioritization that turns them into a roadmap , one that balances stakeholder needs against platform health, survives contact with a changing business, and that your stakeholders can see themselves in. The hard part: saying "not yet" to important people, with a reason they respect.

**Make the Lightdash migration a step-change, not a re-platforming** We're replacing Tableau and Metabase with Lightdash. Done poorly, we trade two messy tools for one messy tool. You'll design the structure, spaces, permissions, certification, naming, that lets stakeholders self-serve at the speed the company needs without creating an uncontrolled dashboard-growth nightmare. The hard part: autonomy and tidiness pull in opposite directions, and you have to deliver both.

**Finish and defend the semantic layer** We just shipped our semantic layer for our most critical metrics, one governed definition per metric, so "two dashboards, two numbers" can't happen. The unglamorous truth: a long tail of metrics still needs definition and mapping, and a semantic layer only stays trustworthy if someone curbs its growth. You'll own both, extending coverage and keeping one-metric-one-definition true as the layer scales.

**Tame event-tracking entropy** Segment events power our funnels and product analytics, and they're implemented by many engineers across many teams. The guardrails exist, a governed event catalog with naming standards, a property dictionary, a review lifecycle, and automated drift detection against production. What's missing is a dedicated owner: someone who holds every new event to the standard, keeps the catalog matched to what production actually sends, and evolves the guardrails as tracking grows. Without that, entropy wins, events drift and silently degrade when features change.

**Get ahead of breakage instead of chasing it** Today, when production data changes upstream, we too often find out when a pipeline breaks or a stakeholder flags a wrong number. You won't start from zero, an AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent already runs freshness monitoring, metric anomaly detection, and dbt-based lineage checks, but it doesn't yet run at the scale or coverage we need. You'll take detection from partial to comprehensive, extend lineage beyond dbt (Segment events and Lightdash need stitching in), and wire it into engineering's change review, so a proposed production change comes with a downstream impact assessment instead of a postmortem. The end-state is data contracts: breaking changes caught in engineering's workflow, not ours.

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

* **Zero pipeline incidents from unannounced source-data changes -** lineage and automation catch them before they break anything downstream, and production changes ship with an impact assessment instead of a postmortem.
* **Zero freshness incidents -** stakeholders never open a stale dashboard.
* **Every area of the business manages on official, well-maintained metrics and dashboards -** product, marketing, ops, and finance self-serve in Lightdash against a fully mapped semantic layer; Tableau and Metabase are retired; arguments about whose number is right don't happen. Not because you built the dashboards **-** because you built the system that keeps them trustworthy.
* **Every Segment event has an owner and a standard -** new events ship compliant, and degradation gets caught automatically, not by accident.
* **Governance runs as a system -** documented processes that would survive you taking a month off.

  
**Requirements**

Who You Are

* **Governance is your craft, not your chore.** You genuinely enjoy making data systems trustworthy and tidy, you're the person who can't leave a broken naming convention alone. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you see governance as a stepping stone to "real" analytics work.
* **AI-native.** You use AI tools (Claude Code, Copilot, ChatGPT) daily to build quality checks, write automation, triage anomalies, and document as you go, one person covering ground that used to take a team. You also see the reverse direction: AI agents consume our data daily, and making the warehouse safe and legible for them is part of governance now. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything manually.
* **A hands-on manager.** You've been accountable for other people's output, allocating their time, owning their priorities, and you never stopped building yourself. You write the SQL, debug the Airflow DAG, and configure the permissions personally. This is unlikely to be a good fit if seniority took you away from the keyboard, or if you've never been responsible for anyone's work but your own.
* **Product-minded.** You start from what the business is trying to decide, not from what the pipeline does, and you can turn a vague stakeholder ask into a prioritized plan. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you need requirements handed to you, or if roadmap conversations feel like a distraction from the real work.
* **Automation-first.** Your instinct for any recurring check is to build a monitor, not a checklist. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your quality practice depends on manual review and discipline.
* **An enforcer people actually like.** You'll hold engineers and analysts you don't manage to standards, which takes clear rules, good tooling that makes compliance easy, and the spine to say no gracefully. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you avoid friction or, at the other extreme, enjoy being the department of no.

This Role Is NOT

* **A big-team leadership role.** You start solo and then hire a Lead Analytics Engineer who reports to you; the team grows only as scope demands. If you want to direct a large org rather than build alongside a small one, this isn't it.
* **A policy or committee job.** There are no governance councils to chair and no binders to produce. When something's broken, you fix it, with code, config, or a conversation.
* **A BI analyst role.** You won't spend your days building dashboards for stakeholders. You build the platform and guardrails that let everyone else do that well.
* **A finished system to babysit.** Much of this doesn't exist yet. If you want to operate a mature data platform rather than build one, you'll be frustrated here.

Tech You'll Touch

* **Warehouse & pipelines** - Redshift, dbt, Airflow
* **Ingestion** - Fivetran, plus custom Airflow pipelines
* **Event tracking** - Segment
* **BI** - Light

jobs.title: Engenheiro(a) de Software Backend Sênior
jobs.description:
**Sobre a vaga**

A nstech está transformando um portfólio logístico formado por aquisições, sistemas legados e funcionalidades sobrepostas em uma plataforma de componentes de negócio reutilizáveis. Buscamos um(a) engenheiro(a) backend sênior para o time de Componentes Transversais, que constrói e mantém os componentes que vários produtos e jornadas compartilham.

Como cada componente atende vários produtos ao mesmo tempo, o trabalho pede atenção especial a contratos estáveis e versionados, isolamento de dados por cliente e evolução sem quebrar quem já consome. A stack principal do time hoje é Node.js com TypeScript e NestJS. A empresa também adota .NET como stack oficial, e o time atua nas duas (conhecimento em .NET será um diferencial).

**Responsabilidades e atribuições**

* Projetar e implementar componentes de negócio expostos por APIs REST e por eventos, escrevendo o contrato (OpenAPI e AsyncAPI) antes do código.
* Evoluir contratos sem quebrar consumidores: mudanças compatíveis, versionamento e publicação em paralelo quando a mudança for incompatível.
* Integrar os componentes à plataforma de dados corporativa (dados mestres e de referência), respeitando a regra de um único dono por dado, sem acesso direto ao banco de outros componentes ou sistemas
* Implementar comunicação assíncrona confiável entre componentes, com outbox, inbox e consumidores idempotentes.
* Modelar a persistência em PostgreSQL com isolamento por cliente (Row-Level Security) e migrations versionadas, aplicadas pelo pipeline.
* Responder pela qualidade e pela operação do que entrega: testes automatizados (unitários, de componente e de contrato), segurança, observabilidade e acompanhamento em produção.
* Participar da migração gradual dos sistemas legados para os novos componentes, cliente a cliente, sempre com caminho de reversão.
* Revisar código, apoiar o time e contribuir com os templates, os padrões e as propostas técnicas (RFCs e ADRs) da engenharia.

**Requisitos e qualificações**

* Experiência sólida em backend com Node.js e TypeScript, construindo e operando serviços em produção, com NestJS ou framework equivalente com injeção de dependência e organização modular.
* Design de APIs REST com contrato versionado (OpenAPI) e tratamento padronizado de erros.
* Mensageria e arquitetura orientada a eventos (Azure Service Bus, RabbitMQ, Kafka ou similar), com domínio de entrega pelo menos uma vez, idempotência e padrão outbox.
* PostgreSQL: modelagem, migrations e desempenho de consultas.
* Testes automatizados no dia a dia, incluindo testes de integração e de contrato.
* Autenticação e autorização em APIs com OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect e JWT, inclusive entre serviços.
* Docker, CI/CD e fluxo de Git baseado em pull request e revisão de código.
* Modelagem orientada a domínio (DDD), com clareza sobre fronteiras, agregados e dono de cada dado.
* Boa escrita técnica em português, para especificações, revisões e propostas.

**Diferenciais**

* C# e .NET.
* Azure (Service Bus, AKS, Key Vault) e Kubernetes, incluindo workers escalados por fila (KEDA) e jobs agendados.
* Multitenancy.
* Keycloak e API gateways, como o Kong.
* gRPC, CloudEvents e AsyncAPI.
* OpenTelemetry, Grafana e Datadog.
* Conhecimento de padrões arquiteturais importantes, como Vertical Slices e CQRS.
* Migração de legado com Strangler Fig, feature flags e rollout por cliente.
* Desenvolvimento assistido por IA, com agentes de código e fluxo orientado a especificação.
* Domínio logístico: TMS, roteirização, embarcador e transportadora.

jobs.title: [Contractor] Pessoa Engenheira de Software Fullstack - Sênior
jobs.description:
Cheesecake Labs é parceira de IA, dados e engenharia de produto para organizações consolidadas e em fase de escala que enfrentam sistemas legados, dados fragmentados, pressão por IA ou capacidade de engenharia limitada.

Nossos serviços incluem Implementação de IA, Modernização de Aplicações, Data & Analytics, Product Engineering, Entrega Acelerada por IA e Times de Engenharia Integrados. Entregamos workflows agênticos em 8 a 12 semanas e modernizamos aplicações em 5 a 10 meses, em vez de 2 anos. Também construímos bases de dados confiáveis e produtos digitais feitos para escalar. Nosso ciclo de desenvolvimento de software agêntico acelera a execução, enquanto engenheiros experientes se integram aos times dos clientes para trazer profundidade técnica, segurança e clareza de ownership.

Membro do Claude Partner Network da Anthropic. Entre nossos parceiros de tecnologia estão Databricks, Snowflake, dbt e AWS.

Em mais de 13 anos, a Cheesecake Labs construiu mais de 300 produtos para clientes como Eurasia Group, MoneyGram, World Bank, Stellar, Wedgewood, PepsiCo, Merck, Sodexo e Mercado Libre.

  

### **Detalhes da contratação**

* Modelo de contractor, por projeto
* Pagamento por hora
* 100% remoto
* Alocação flexível, conforme a disponibilidade de projetos e o fit
* As oportunidades podem variar em duração, escopo e dedicação semanal, de acordo com as necessidades dos clientes

Algumas oportunidades podem começar imediatamente.  
Outras podem ser ativadas conforme novos projetos entrarem no nosso pipeline.

  

### **A história por trás desta vaga**

  

Muitas vagas de engenharia de IA ainda giram em torno de experimentos, protótipos isolados ou pesquisa. Esta não é uma delas.

Na Cheesecake Labs, construímos software e soluções com IA para empresas reais, com usuários reais, restrições reais e prazos reais. Nossos squads são pequenos e seniores, e entregam em semanas e meses, não em anos.

Hoje, agentes de IA escrevem a maior parte do nosso código. Esta vaga é para quem decide como as coisas são construídas, direciona os agentes, verifica o resultado e responde por ele diante do cliente.

Estamos buscando uma pessoa Engenheira de Software Sênior: alguém que assume um projeto de cliente desde a primeira conversa de escopo até a produção, e que lida com as decisões de negócio, produto e técnica no caminho. Quando o projeto tem PM, a direção de produto fica com essa pessoa e você é a contraparte técnica dela. Quando não tem, você recebe o problema direto do founder ou do cliente.

  

### **Como é esta vaga na prática**

Esta não é uma vaga de “receber tickets e implementar features”. Também não é uma vaga de “escrever cada linha na mão”.

Em um projeto típico, você pode:

* Rodar o nosso Spec Driven, nosso fluxo de desenvolvimento orientado a specs: reunir contexto, especificar, planejar, implementar por meio de agentes de IA, revisar e fechar o ciclo.
* Transformar um problema de negócio do cliente em um desenho técnico e em uma spec que um agente de IA consiga executar e que você consiga verificar.
* Trabalhar com PM, designer e o squad para entender o que deve ser construído, ou receber os requisitos direto do founder ou do cliente quando não há PM.
* Participar de conversas com o cliente sobre objetivos, escopo e trade-offs técnicos, e mantê-lo atualizado por escrito ao longo do caminho.
* Direcionar agentes de IA (Claude Code, Cursor ou similares) para implementar a partir da sua spec. Escrever código à mão é a exceção, não o padrão.
* Revisar o que os agentes produzem, combinando loops automatizados de revisão com a sua própria checagem de arquitetura e comportamento, e responder por 100% do que é entregue.
* Tomar as decisões de arquitetura. A IA executa, você decide.
* Entregar e iterar, e depois fechar o ciclo devolvendo decisões e edge cases ao contexto do projeto, para que a próxima spec comece mais bem informada.
* Usar todos os dias o nosso harness compartilhado (skills, agentes e loops de revisão), melhorá-lo e devolver o que funciona, para que todos os squads se beneficiem.
* Trabalhar dentro das regras de cada cliente sobre o uso de IA (veja Como usamos IA aqui).

Alguns projetos pesam mais na arquitetura. Outros, nas conversas com o cliente. A maioria mistura os dois. Você trabalha com bastante autonomia, e conta com um Engineering Manager e com o squad quando precisar.

  

### **O que costuma funcionar bem por aqui**

Quem se destaca nesta vaga costuma:

* Ter construído e entregue produtos de software reais de ponta a ponta, com JS/Typescript, e/ou Python, e conseguir explicar as decisões que tomou.
* Já usar agentes de IA todos os dias para projetar, construir, depurar e pesquisar, e conseguir mostrar o que construiu.
* Pensar em specs: transformar ambiguidade em definições estruturadas e testáveis.
* Ter mentalidade full-stack. Backend, frontend, IA ou produto podem ser o seu forte, e você circula entre as camadas quando o projeto precisa.
* Verificar antes de dizer “pronto” e deixar claro o que foi e o que não foi verificado.
* Trazer problemas cedo, já com opções, e compartilhar o que aprendeu com o time.
* Atuar bem com alta autonomia, pouca burocracia e ciclos rápidos de feedback, em um formato 100% remoto.

  

### **Talvez esta vaga não seja para você se**

Só para ser transparente:

* Você precisa de requisitos detalhados ou de direção constante antes de começar.
* Você vê a IA como ferramenta de apoio, ou prefere escrever a maior parte do código à mão.
* Você se sente confortável entregando resultado de IA que não verificou.
* Você prefere funções focadas só em implementação, sem conversa com cliente ou com o negócio.
* Você não se sente à vontade conversando direto com clientes ou lidando com problemas ambíguos.
* Você tende a ficar em silêncio entre o kickoff e a entrega.
* Você prefere prioridades estáveis a iteração rápida e alta ownership.

Não há nada de errado em nenhuma dessas preferências. Só não é assim que a gente trabalha.

  

### **Uma última coisa**

Para participar deste processo seletivo, você precisa:

* Ter um registro empresarial válido no seu país (CNPJ, VAT, EIN ou equivalente).
* Ter uma conta bancária apta a receber pagamentos em seu registro empresarial.
* Poder emitir invoices (notas fiscais ou equivalente) conforme necessário.

Esses requisitos são necessários para a contratação como prestador de serviços (contractor) e para o processamento dos pagamentos.

  

### **Não tem certeza se atende a todos os requisitos?**

Tudo bem.

Sabemos que muitas pessoas excelentes, principalmente de grupos sub-representados, hesitam em se candidatar quando não atendem a 100% dos requisitos. Se esta oportunidade te interessa, queremos te conhecer mesmo assim.

**DICA IMPORTANTE:** a comunicação durante o processo seletivo é feita por e-mail. Sugerimos que você fique de olho na sua caixa de entrada e libere o recebimento de mensagens de @cheesecakelabs.hire.trakstar.com, para que nossas mensagens não caiam no spam ;)

### **Como usamos IA aqui**

Na Cheesecake Labs, agentes de IA fazem a maior parte da execução: código, infraestrutura, modelos de dados, pesquisa, protótipos e documentação. As pessoas tomam as decisões: o que será construído e em que ordem, a arquitetura, a alocação dos times e qualquer assunto que envolva pessoas. Todas as vagas aqui especificam, direcionam a IA, verificam o resultado e respondem pelo que é entregue.

Em todos os projetos, também seguimos algumas regras:

* Usar apenas ferramentas aprovadas, por meio das contas corporativas da Cheesecake Labs.
* Seguir as regras de cada cliente sobre IA. Alguns clientes exigem uma stack de IA específica, e mercados altamente regulados (como o setor bancário no Brasil) podem exigir modelos hospedados no país.
* Nunca inserir dados de clientes ou dados pessoais (nomes, datas de nascimento, e-mails) em uma LLM sem antes anonimizá-los. O mesmo vale para os dados das nossas próprias pessoas.
* Cumprir a LGPD e as demais leis de proteção de dados aplicáveis.

  

*Os dados pessoais coletados serão usados apenas para gerenciar e controlar os currículos das pessoas candidatas, a fim de avaliar os requisitos necessários, como as informações de contato, e também para conduzir este processo seletivo.*

*Os dados coletados não serão compartilhados com terceiros sem a sua autorização, e seu uso será restrito à equipe interna da Cheesecake Labs e aos prestadores de serviço que processam seus dados para o processo seletivo. A qualquer momento, você pode entrar em contato conosco e removeremos seus dados do nosso sistema de coleta de dados. Para isso, basta enviar um e-mail para* ***careers@cheesecakelabs.com******.***

jobs.title: Arquiteto de Solução Especialista em SuperApp & Inteligência Aplicada
jobs.description:
Especialista em Arquitetura de Soluções TI – SuperApp & Smart Experience (Mobile + AI) O que faz a área de Arquitetura de Soluções no Projeto SuperApp Porto? A área de Arquitetura tem papel central no redesign e consolidação do SuperApp Porto, unificando as verticais de Seguros, Banco e Serviços em uma experiência única, inteligente, fluida e altamente performática. Como Arquiteto(a) de Solução Especialista em SuperApp & Inteligência Aplicada, você será o guardião técnico da estratégia mobile e da camada de inteligência da Porto. Sua missão será desenhar uma arquitetura modular, escalável, segura e inteligente.
  
  
Você garantirá que as três verticais evoluam suas funcionalidades de forma desacoplada, utilizando capacidades de IA Generativa, Agentes Inteligentes e Modelos On-Device/Cloud para personalizar jornadas, hiper-personalizar serviços financeiros e de seguros e oferecer assistência proativa e contextualizada aos clientes. Principais Stakeholders: Arquitetos Corporativos, Arquitetos de Software Mobile e Especialistas em Data/AI; Líderes Técnicos e Engenheiros Mobile (iOS, Android, React Native/Flutter) e Backend; Tech Leads e Product Owners (POs) das verticais de Seguros, Banco e Serviços; Times de AI Engineering, Data Platform, Design System, UX/UI, Segurança da Informação e MLOps; Parcerias de Negócio e Inovação das Verticais. Seus Principais Desafios no SuperApp serão: 1. Arquitetura Modular de SuperApp & Mini-Apps: Definir a estratégia de modularização móvel (SuperApp / Mini-Apps / Micro-frontends Mobile), permitindo o desenvolvimento e deploy independente das verticais de Seguros, Banco e Serviços sem comprometer a estabilidade do app base.
  
  
**2. Orquestração de Inteligência Artificial no SuperApp:** Projetar a arquitetura de integração entre o ecossistema móvel e os serviços de IA/LLM/GenAI da Porto, habilitando assistentes virtuais contextuais, busca semântica em apólices/serviços, recomendação preditiva de produtos bancários/seguros e automação inteligente de sinistros e solicitações. 3. Equilíbrio de IA On-Device x Cloud AI: Avaliar e arquitetar estratégias de IA que rodem diretamente no dispositivo móvel (On-Device AI / Small Language Models - SLMs) para inferências ultra-rápidas e privacidade (ex: biometria contextual, privacidade offline) combinadas com modelos avançados baseados em Cloud (RAG / Agentic Workflows).
  
  
**4. Resiliência, Performance e Otimização Móvel:** Garantir inicialização rápida (Cold/Warm Start), baixo consumo de bateria e memória, resiliência em redes instáveis (Offline-First) e controle de latência nas chamadas de chamadas de APIs de IA/LLM. 5. Governança de Integração Móvel (BFF & Server-Driven UI): Padronizar a camada de APIs móveis usando Backend-For-Frontend (BFF), GraphQL/REST e Server-Driven UI (SDUI), permitindo atualizar fluxos e interfaces impulsionadas por IA dinamicamente, sem a necessidade de reenvio de compilações às lojas.
  
  
**6. Segurança Móvel, Privacidade de Dados e IA Responsável:** Garantir proteção avançada para transações financeiras e dados sensíveis (OAuth2/PKCE, SSL Pinning, App Shielding, Passkeys), alinhando a captura de contexto de uso do app com governança de dados, LGPD, mascaramento de PII em prompts de LLM e IA Responsável. Requisitos e Qualificações (O que você precisa para fazer parte deste time): 1. Formação e Padrões de Arquitetura: Superior completo em Tecnologia, Ciência da Computação, Engenharia de Software ou áreas correlatas; Pós-graduação ou especialização em Arquitetura de Software, Soluções Móveis, Ciência de Dados ou Inteligência Artificial; Domínio de padrões de arquitetura de software (Clean Architecture, Hexagonal, DDD) e padrões móveis (VIPER, MVVM-C, MVI).
  
  
**2. Competências Técnicas em Mobile & SuperApps (Hard Skills):** Arquitetura de SuperApp / Micro-frontends Mobile: Sólida experiência no desenho de plataformas móveis modulares baseadas em arquiteturas extensoras (Mini-Apps, Module Federation, Dynamic Feature Modules no Android e Frameworks no iOS); Tecnologias Mobile: Experiência prática em ecossistemas de desenvolvimento mobile nativo (Swift/iOS, Kotlin/Android) e/ou híbridos/cross-platform (React Native, Flutter); Integração & APIs: Domínio em padrões BFF (Backend-For-Frontend), GraphQL, RESTful APIs, gRPC e Server-Driven UI (SDUI); Resiliência e Performance Client-Side: Experiência em estratégias de caching local (SQLite, Realm, Room, CoreData), sincronização offline-first e otimização de payloads; Segurança Mobile & Identidade: Experiência com OAuth2/OIDC (PKCE), mTLS, SSL/TLS Pinning, armazenamento seguro (Keystore/Keychain), biometria (FaceID/TouchID, Passkeys), encriptação local e mecanismos anti-tampering; Observabilidade & Esteira Mobile: Monitoramento de performance e erros client-side (Datadog Mobile RUM, Firebase Crashlytics, Sentry) e automação de testes/deploy (Fastlane, Bitrise, GitHub Actions, Feature Flags, Phased Rollout). Gestão de Identidade e Acesso (CIAM) & Segurança: Experiência prática ou arquitetural em plataformas de identidade como ForgeRock, projetando fluxos de autenticação unificada (Single Sign-On - SSO), autorização (OAuth2/OIDC com PKCE), gerenciamento de sessões, autenticação adaptativa e consentimentos transversais no SuperApp. Integração de APIs e Sistemas Legados: Domínio em arquiteturas de integração híbrida e gestão de APIs via iPaaS (MuleSoft Anypoint Platform), orquestrando o desacoplamento de sistemas legados/core das verticais com as APIs expostas para a camada de BFF do SuperApp.
  
  
**Infraestrutura em Nuvem (Cloud Native):** Domínio em serviços da AWS (como Elastic Kubernetes Service - EKS, AWS Lambda/Serverless, API Gateway, DynamoDB, S3, CloudFront) para suporte à camada móvel de altíssimo tráfego, resiliência e baixa latência. 3. jobs.description:
**About Workato**
=================

Workato is the leading Control and Execution Platform for Enterprise AI — the neutral platform enterprises trust to put AI to work across their business. Workato unifies data, applications, and processes into a single platform so AI can reliably orchestrate business processes in production at enterprise scale. Built on more than a decade of running mission-critical processes for over half the Fortune 500 — including Nasdaq, Amazon, Cisco, Vodafone, Atlassian, and Lucid Motors — Workato turns over 14,000 enterprise systems AI needs to act on into one governed execution layer. For more information, visit workato.com.

**Why join us?**
================

Ultimately, Workato believes in fostering a **flexible, trust-oriented culture that empowers everyone to take full ownership of their roles**. We are driven by **innovation** and looking for **team players** who want to actively build our company.

But, we also believe in **balancing productivity with self-care**. That's why we offer all of our employees a vibrant and dynamic work environment along with a multitude of benefits they can enjoy inside and outside of their work lives.

If this sounds right up your alley, please submit an application. We look forward to getting to know you!

Also, feel free to check out why:

* Business Insider named us an "enterprise startup to bet your career on"
* Forbes' Cloud 100 recognized us as one of the top 100 private cloud companies in the world
* Deloitte Tech Fast 500 ranked us as the 17th fastest growing tech company in the Bay Area, and 96th in North America
* Quartz ranked us the #1 best company for remote workers

**About the role**
==================

Workato is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the ChatBots and AI team within our Platform organization. This is a high-ownership role for someone who thrives in ambiguity: you turn unclear requirements into clear execution plans, make confident decisions with incomplete information, and keep both the team and leadership aligned. The team is fully remote and international - you'll build the processes and culture that make it work at pace.

### **About the Team**

The ChatBots and AI team's mission is to deliver AI agents to end users. We own the runtime and integration layer - conversation storage, API design, streaming, and integrations with external interfaces like Slack and other applications. The team is made up of Senior and Staff engineers working in Ruby/Rails and Go on a modern stack: PostgreSQL, Kafka, Redis, Kubernetes, and AWS. You'll collaborate with dedicated QA, SRE, and UX/UI teams, as well as engineering teams across the broader organization. Workato has a strong cross-functional culture - your team won't work in isolation.

### **What You'll Do**

**Delivery**

* Partner with Product Managers and stakeholders to scope projects, set timelines, and define what success looks like
* Plan and track execution across quarters and sprints; deliver on schedule without compromising quality
* Identify blockers early, resolve them decisively, and escalate when escalation is the right call
* Balance feature work against internal investments - AI-SDLC, CI/CD, platform upgrades, and technical debt

**Team**

* Manage, mentor, and grow a team of Senior and Staff engineers
* Own hiring, onboarding, and performance management
* Design team processes that fit a distributed, asynchronous environment - and evolve them as the team and company change
* Apply AI tooling to how the team works, not just what it builds

**Technical Ownership**

* Participate in architecture and design decisions as a technical peer to your engineers
* Make trade-off calls on scope, approach, and sequencing - and be accountable for them
* Understand the system deeply enough to allocate the team's capacity where it matters most

**Communication**

* Keep leadership informed on progress, risks, and blockers with clarity and without spin
* Build working relationships with peer leads across engineering and product
* Represent your team's priorities and constraints in cross-team planning

**Requirements**
================

* 5+ years managing engineering teams, including Senior and Staff-level individual contributors
* Senior engineer-level technical depth - you can read the code, challenge a design, and hold your own in an architecture discussion
* Hands-on background in backend engineering; experience with Ruby, Go, or comparable languages and distributed systems
* Demonstrated ability to operate under ambiguity: defining direction where none exists, and committing to decisions before all the information is available
* Track record of shipping complex software on schedule in a fast-moving environment
* Experience managing a fully remote, distributed team across multiple time zones
* Strong written communication - in an async environment, writing is the primary management tool

### **Nice to Have**

* Experience building AI-powered products - agents, LLM pipelines, or orchestration systems
* Background in platform, integration, or developer-facing infrastructure
* Experience scaling a team through periods of rapid growth
* Familiarity with enterprise SaaS or automation platforms

jobs.title: Lead Analytics Engineer, Data Governance & Platform
jobs.description:
**About LawnStarter**
---------------------

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services, operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

**About Analytics at LawnStarter**
----------------------------------

We're a small, senior analytics team supporting the entire company: product, marketing, operations, and finance all run on the data we serve. The foundation is solid. A centralized Redshift data warehouse holds all source data, modeled in dbt and orchestrated by Airflow, with Segment feeding event data in. You won't be stitching scattered sources together. The platform exists, and your job is to make it trustworthy and keep it that way. We're mid-migration to Lightdash as our single BI platform, replacing Tableau and Metabase.

Data governance is becoming a dedicated function here. You'll be its first dedicated owner, building it alongside the Data Director.

**The Role**
------------

You'll own LawnStarter's data governance area and build it: the person who turns the governance agenda into working systems (monitors, checks, lineage, metric definitions, tracking standards) with your own hands. You'll grow the function together with the Data Director, at the pace demand and impact call for. If you want it and the skills are there, you could become its manager one day.

"Lead" here means technical weight first. You're the reference the analysts turn to when a pipeline misbehaves, a metric definition gets contentious, or an event's data looks wrong, and the example that raises the bar for how governance work gets done. As the function grows, your leadership can widen with it.

**What makes this role different:**

* **Build, don't chase.** Your job is the machinery that catches data problems before stakeholders do: automation and monitors, not manual firefighting.
* **Whole-stack surface.** Source data to pipelines to dashboards and ML models. Your work touches the entire chain, not one slice of it.
* **A live migration to shape.** Lightdash is landing now, and the semantic layer just shipped for our most critical metrics. You'll do the defining, mapping, and tidying work that decides whether they stay trustworthy.
* **An area to grow.** Governance doesn't have a fixed shape here yet. You'll decide with the Data Director what the function takes on next and how it grows.

**What You'll Own**
-------------------

* **Quality and freshness machinery,** building and scaling the automated monitoring (freshness checks, schema-change alerts, anomaly monitors) that catches upstream changes before they break anything downstream, and running incidents to resolution.
* **Semantic-layer coverage,** the long tail of metrics that still needs definition and mapping, done to the one-metric-one-definition standard, plus the hygiene that keeps the layer tidy as it grows.
* **Event-catalog operations,** reviewing new Segment events against our governed catalog's standards, keeping the catalog matched to what production actually sends, and investigating drift when detection flags it.
* **Lineage tooling,** extending our lineage map beyond dbt (Segment events and Lightdash need stitching in) so downstream impact of a production change can be assessed before it ships.
* **Lightdash hygiene,** the hands-on side of workspace health: certification, naming, permissions upkeep, and keeping self-serve content findable and trustworthy.
* **The data roadmap, increasingly,** working with the Data Director to turn what product, marketing, ops, and finance need from data into priorities for the platform, and owning more of that roadmap as the function grows.

Scope here widens with demand and with what your work proves. As the function takes on more, more of it becomes yours to run, including helping hire the people it adds.

**Problems to Solve**
---------------------

**Take detection from partial to comprehensive** An AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent already runs freshness monitoring, dbt job monitoring, and dbt-based lineage checks, but not yet at the scale or coverage we need. You'll extend it until "a stakeholder found the problem first" stops happening.

**Map the long tail of the semantic layer** Our most critical metrics have one governed definition each, in code. Well over a hundred more still need defining and mapping: unglamorous, high-judgment work where every shortcut becomes someone's wrong number later.

**Keep the event catalog honest** Segment events are implemented by many engineers across many teams, and entropy is relentless: new events drift from standards, and existing ones silently degrade when features change. The guardrails exist. You're the person who runs them and catches what they miss.

**Turn business needs into a data roadmap** Every area of the company wants something from data, and today those asks reach the Analytics team as a stream of interruptions. With the Data Director, you'll turn them into priorities that balance stakeholder needs against platform health. The hard part: saying "not yet" to important people, with a reason they respect.

**What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**
------------------------------------

* **The monitors you built catch problems before stakeholders do,** pipeline and freshness incidents get found by automation, not by someone opening a stale dashboard.
* **The semantic layer's long tail is mapped,** every reported metric has exactly one governed definition, and arguments about whose number is right don't happen.
* **Event reviews run on a steady cadence,** new events ship compliant, drift gets investigated within days, and the catalog matches production.
* **You're the acknowledged technical reference,** when something data-related looks wrong anywhere in the company, people know who to bring it to, and you usually already know.
* **Data-trust asks come to you,** stakeholders bring their data-quality and governance requests to you directly, and you hold a slice of the roadmap with the Data Director.

  
**Requirements**  

**Who You Are**
---------------

* **Governance is your craft, not your chore.** You enjoy making data systems trustworthy and tidy. You're the person who can't leave a broken naming convention alone. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you see governance as a stepping stone to "real" analytics work.
* **AI-native.** You use AI tools (Claude Code, Copilot, ChatGPT) daily to build quality checks, write automation, triage anomalies, and document as you go. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI tools or prefer to do everything manually.
* **A hands-on builder at a lead bar.** You write the SQL, debug the Airflow DAG, and ship the monitor yourself, and the way you do it becomes the way the team does it. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your instinct is to spec work for someone else to execute.
* **Automation-first.** Your instinct for any recurring check is to build a monitor, not a checklist. This is unlikely to be a good fit if your quality practice depends on manual review and discipline.
* **A technical reference people seek out.** You explain clearly, answer patiently, and leave people smarter. Your influence comes from that, before any title does. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you need formal authority to get people to follow a standard.
* **Open to growing with the function.** If the area grows into a team and leading it suits you, you're open to developing the management side to get there. If it doesn't, staying the technical lead of this area is a full, senior role here, not a consolation prize. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you'd take the role mainly for the title it might lead to.

**This Role Is NOT**
--------------------

* **A BI analyst role.** You won't spend your days building dashboards for stakeholders. You build the machinery that keeps everyone else's dashboards trustworthy.
* **A title with a timeline, or a guarantee.** There's no promotion date. If the role grows into managing the function, the Manager title follows the work you're already doing. If the function needs a manager before that happens, or the fit isn't there, we'd hire one, and you'd remain the technical lead of the area.
* **A hands-off role.** The building is the job now, and it stays core as your scope grows. If you want to step away from the keyboard, this isn't it.

**Tech You'll Touch**
---------------------

* **Warehouse & pipelines -** Redshift, dbt, Airflow
* **Ingestion -** Fivetran, plus custom Airflow pipelines
* **Event tracking** - Segment
* **BI** - Lightdash (primary), Tableau and Metabase (sunsetting)
* **AI tooling** - Claude Code, Codex, Brain (our internal AI toolkit), and any tool that makes you more effective or efficient
* **Observability** - an AI-powered Analytics Engineer agent (freshness monitoring, dbt job monitoring, dbt lineage) you'll extend, plus the quality and impact tooling you'll build around it

You don't need every box checked. You need hands-on depth in the warehouse/pipeline layer and the instinct to automate what others check manually.

 **Benefits**  

* **Base salary**: $75k–$100k/year (contractor arrangement, standard for our Latin America-based team; no equity)
* **Fully remote**: This work needs deep focus, building monitors, untangling pipelines, and we trust you to manage your environment. Async collaboration is the norm.
* **Flexible PTO**: We focus on results. Take what you need.

*LawnStarter provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetics. We comply with applicable state and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment.*

jobs.title: Tech Lead
jobs.description:
Enumerate is hiring a **Lead Full Stack AI Engineer (Tech Lead)** to lead the technical development of AI-powered product capabilities. This is a deeply hands-on engineering role for an experienced full-stack developer who has built production applications using Large Language Models (LLMs), understands modern AI application architectures, and brings strong data engineering instincts. The Tech Lead will be responsible for both defining the technical approach and personally implementing critical parts of the solution. This is not a management-only or architecture-only position. The successful candidate will write production code daily while providing technical direction, mentoring developers, and ensuring high-quality execution across a small, fast-moving AI Pod. The role works closely with Product Management and Platform leadership to translate product opportunities into reliable, scalable AI-powered features.

This is a remote contractor opportunity for candidates located in LATAM who are comfortable working in an English-speaking professional environment.

**Key Responsibilities**

AI Solution Delivery & Architecture

* Lead the design, implementation, and production deployment of AI-powered product features using LLMs and modern AI application architectures.

* Architect and personally develop LLM integrations, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipelines, embeddings, vector search, and tool/function calling capabilities.

* Design and implement agentic workflows that combine LLM reasoning, enterprise data retrieval, business logic, and application actions.

* Make informed architectural decisions regarding model selection, orchestration frameworks, context management, and retrieval strategies.

* Build reusable AI services and components that can support multiple product features.

* Implement robust error handling, fallbacks, human-in-the-loop controls, and safeguards for AI-driven workflows.

* Optimize AI systems for accuracy, reliability, latency, scalability, and cost.

* Evaluate emerging AI frameworks and capabilities, selecting technologies based on practical product and engineering needs.

Data Architecture & AI integration

* Design data access and retrieval architectures that enable AI applications to operate reliably on enterprise data.

* Work across relational databases, data lakes, APIs, and structured/unstructured data sources.

* Understand data lake and lakehouse architectures, ingestion patterns, transformation pipelines, and analytical data models.

* Apply strong judgment around data quality, lineage, freshness, consistency, and authoritative sources.

* Design retrieval strategies that combine structured queries, semantic search, and application-specific business logic.

* Collaborate with Data Engineering to establish reliable, governed data access patterns for AI applications.

* Ensure appropriate data security, access controls, and privacy safeguards when integrating enterprise data with LLMs.

* Identify and address data quality or architectural limitations that could affect AI accuracy and reliability.

AI Quality, Evaluation and Operational Excellence

* Establish practical evaluation and testing approaches for LLM-powered features, including response quality, grounding, correctness, and regression testing.

* Implement observability for AI workflows, including model usage, latency, token consumption, cost, failures, and application-level outcomes.

* Design mechanisms to detect and mitigate hallucinations, unreliable outputs, and inappropriate AI actions.

* Implement appropriate human approval, auditability, and explainability mechanisms for AI-assisted decisions.

* Ensure AI functionality operates securely and reliably within existing application and cloud infrastructure.

* Drive continuous improvement through production telemetry, user feedback, and experimentation.

* Establish reusable engineering patterns for testing, deploying, and operating AI-enabled features.

Pod Leadership & Execution

* Act as the technical lead for a cross-functional AI Pod.

* Break down product requirements into executable technical workstreams and prototypes.

* Guide rapid iteration cycles, proofs-of-concept, and MVPs, balancing experimentation with production readiness.

* Review code, architecture, and technical decisions to maintain quality and velocity.

Product & Data Collaboration

* Partner closely with Product Management to shape problem definitions, success metrics, and delivery plans.

* Collaborate with the Product Leader to integrate models, analytics, and data assets into product workflows.

* Translate Data outputs into consumable APIs, services, and product features.

* Provide technical feedback on feasibility, scope, and tradeoffs during product discovery.

Operationalization & Quality

* Ensure features are production-grade, including monitoring, logging, and performance tracking.

* Implement guardrails around AI usage, including reliability, latency, cost controls, and failure modes.

* Support experimentation frameworks, A/B testing, and post-launch learning loops.

* Drive responsible AI practices, including explainability, bias awareness, and data privacy considerations.

Technical Standards & Enablement

* Define and enforce lightweight engineering standards for AI-enabled systems.

* Promote reuse of components, prompts, pipelines, and services across AI initiatives.

* Mentor pod engineers on AI-adjacent system design and best practices.

* Contribute to internal documentation and shared AI patterns/playbooks.

**Required Qualifications**

* 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, including significant hands-on development of production applications.

* Strong full-stack engineering capabilities, including modern frontend frameworks such as React or Vue and backend development using Python, Node.js, Java, or similar technologies.

* Demonstrated experience designing, building, and shipping production LLM-powered applications or AI-enabled product features.

* Strong practical knowledge of the modern LLM application stack, including prompting, RAG, embeddings, vector search, model APIs, and tool/function calling.

* Experience designing AI application architectures that integrate LLMs, backend services, enterprise data, and business workflows.

* Strong understanding of databases, data modeling, data pipelines, and data lake concepts.

* Ability to design reliable data retrieval and integration patterns for AI applications.

* Experience designing and building scalable APIs, backend services, and cloud-native applications.

* Strong software engineering fundamentals, including automated testing, observability, debugging, and production operations.

* Experience providing technical leadership through architecture decisions, code reviews, mentoring, and hands-on collaboration.

* Demonstrated ability to independently solve complex technical problems while remaining an active individual contributor.

* Experience working closely with Product teams in fast-moving, iterative environments.

* BS/MS in Computer Science, Engineering, or related discipline, or equivalent practical experience.

  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience designing and implementing agentic AI systems, including multi-step workflows, tool orchestration, and human-in-the-loop patterns.

* Familiarity with LLM frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, LangGraph, or similar technologies.

* Experience with AI evaluation frameworks, model observability, prompt/version management, and production AI monitoring.

* Experience with AWS data and AI services, including S3, Athena, Glue, Bedrock, or comparable technologies.

* Familiarity with data lakehouse architectures and medallion data patterns.

* Experience combining structured data retrieval, SQL, and semantic search in AI applications.

* Experience building AI capabilities within enterprise SaaS applications.

* Experience with workflow orchestration frameworks such as Temporal or similar technologies.

* Familiarity with AI security considerations, including prompt injection, data leakage, and permission-aware retrieval.

* Experience leading small engineering teams while remaining a substantial individual contributor.

**What Success Looks Like**

* Personally deliver complex AI-powered product features while guiding a small team of developers.

* Establish a pragmatic, reusable technical foundation for LLM-powered and agentic product capabilities.

* Build reliable integrations between AI models, enterprise data, and existing application workflows.

* Make sound architectural decisions that balance delivery speed, AI quality, scalability, and operational cost.

* Raise the technical capabilities and productivity of pod developers through hands-on mentoring and collaboration.

* Deliver production AI features that are secure, observable, maintainable, and demonstrably valuable to customers.

**Prazer, somos a Platform Builders!**
--------------------------------------

Somos um ecossistema de tecnologia e inovação que ajuda empresas a construir bases tecnológicas sólidas, com a Inteligência Artificial no centro das soluções. Já participamos de mais de 300 projetos com grandes empresas de diferentes segmentos.

Em cada um deles, buscamos entender os desafios e encontrar as soluções que fazem mais sentido. Mas a tecnologia é só uma parte dessa história. Nosso propósito é gerar impacto positivo nas pessoas e nos negócios, e acreditamos que isso começa com quem constrói tudo junto com a gente.

Se você procura um ambiente em que possa aprender, contribuir e crescer junto com outras pessoas, queremos conhecer você!

**Antes de avançar, o que você precisa saber?**
-----------------------------------------------

* **Contratação:** CLT.
* **Modelo de trabalho:** remoto.
* **Horário:** das 9h às 12h e das 13h às 18h, com flexibilidade para organizar a rotina de acordo com as agendas e as entregas.

**Agora, vamos falar sobre a vaga?**
------------------------------------

Estamos em busca de uma pessoa para fazer parte do nosso time como **Desenvolvedor(a) Especialista Front-end (React)**!

Nesta posição, você vai atuar em um cliente de grande porte, com plataformas web e e-commerce de alto tráfego. Não procuramos alguém para executar tarefas já definidas, e sim uma referência técnica, que vai conhecer as plataformas a fundo, montar um diagnóstico completo e ser owner da evolução delas, unindo visão de arquitetura, olhar de segurança e mão na massa. Também vai propor caminhos e, quando for preciso, questionar direcionamentos com base em dados e argumentos técnicos.

**E como será o seu dia a dia?**
--------------------------------

Na prática, sua rotina vai envolver:

* Levantar problemas, riscos e oportunidades de melhoria, com prioridade definida por criticidade e esforço.
* Transformar esse diagnóstico em um plano de ação e um roadmap de evolução, deixando claros os ganhos de cada iniciativa.

* Desenvolver e evoluir aplicações em React e Next.js, com foco em qualidade, performance e escalabilidade.

**O que você precisa ter?**

* Experiência sólida com React em produção, em aplicações de alta complexidade e alto volume de acessos.

* Experiência com arquitetura front-end e otimização de performance (ex.: code splitting, lazy loading, memoization e Core Web Vitals).

* Conhecimento de segurança em aplicações web (ex.: OWASP Top 10, XSS, CSRF, CSP, autenticação e proteção de fluxos sensíveis).
* Conhecimento de APIs REST, microsserviços e mensageria, o suficiente para diagnosticar gargalos e orientar soluções com o back-end.
* Experiência com gerenciamento de estado (ex.: TanStack Query, Redux ou Zustand).
* Experiência com testes automatizados (ex.: Jest, Vitest, React Testing Library, Cypress ou Playwright), ferramentas de build e pipelines de CI/CD.
* Experiência conduzindo diagnósticos técnicos, refatorações relevantes ou planos de evolução de aplicações.
* Comunicação forte, com capacidade de conversar com pessoas de áreas diferentes, defender posições técnicas e influenciar decisões.
* Perfil de ownership e autonomia, com conforto para atuar entre a estratégia e a execução.

**Será um diferencial se você tiver:**

jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, Product
jobs.description:
**About LawnStarter**

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care to become the one-stop shop for all home services — operating across three brands (LawnStarter, Lawn Love, Home Gnome) on a single shared platform.

**About Engineering at LawnStarter**

We build in small, focused initiative teams: a Product Engineer working alongside a PM and a designer, supported by an Engineering Manager who helps you grow. You'll also work shoulder-to-shoulder with engineering peers across initiatives in a shared codebase. The whole team owns whether the work moves its metric.

AI coding agents are a force multiplier here — they give a small, senior team the leverage to ship more, faster, and at a higher bar for quality. We hire engineers who are wired for ownership and energized by shipping to a real marketplace with customers and pros on both sides.

**The Role**

You're the engineering anchor of an initiative — working as part of a tight team with your PM and designer, and alongside engineering peers on adjacent initiatives. You have a hand in the full lifecycle: shaping the problem, deciding the technical approach, directing AI agents to implement much of the code, shipping to production, and — with your team — owning the outcome.

You're measured by impact, not by lines of code merged. When an agent can ship something safely, your job is to make sure it's done right and the metric moves. When the work touches a sensitive area, you have the guardrails to prove the change does exactly what it should, with no side effects: strong tests, evals, staged rollouts, and review gates.

**What makes this role exciting:**

* **You ship end-to-end.** From problem-framing through production to the post-launch metric review — you see the whole arc and own the result with your team.
* **You work as a true product partner.** You sit at the table with PM and design, bringing engineering judgment to product calls and product sense to engineering calls.
* **You get real autonomy — with the right checkpoints.** You make most technical calls yourself, with architect review on significant architectural decisions and fast input from peers.
* **You operate at a staff bar.** You're trusted to make the call, ship the hard thing, and stand behind the outcome.

### **What You'll Own**

* **The technical approach** — architecture, data model, integration choices, rollout plan, observability, and rollback strategy for your initiative. You make most calls yourself and bring significant architectural decisions to architect review; you document them, and revisit if the data says you were wrong.
* **Implementation quality** — the prompts, guardrails, evals, tests, and review loop that let agents ship safe, correct, production-ready code. Most lines will be agent-authored, and you're accountable for them — held to the same standard as the rest of the team working in a shared codebase.
* **Cross-functional partnership** — daily working contact with your PM (scope, tradeoffs) and designer (UX decisions, in-tool prototyping), regular collaboration with engineering peers, and weekly check-ins with your EM.
* **The initiative outcome** — the metric the initiative was set up to move. With your PM, you present results 2–4 weeks post-launch and share the "did it work" answer.
* **A high bar for what ships** — production correctness, security, performance, observability, and the experience for customers and pros. Agents accelerate you; they don't lower the bar.

### **Problems to Solve**

**Leading AI agents at a staff-level quality bar** Most of the code on your initiative will be authored by AI agents. The craft is making them ship as if a senior engineer wrote it: prompts that encode our conventions, evals that catch issues before merge, tests that exercise the edges, observability that catches a regression before a customer does. How do you build a workflow that lets a small team ship far more than its size would suggest?

**Owning decisions with high autonomy** You have real latitude to make and document technical calls quickly — with architect review on the big architectural ones and peers to pressure-test your thinking. How do you move fast, keep your team aligned, and stay accountable to the outcome?

**Shipping outcomes, not features** Each initiative is measured by a metric — a conversion rate, a retention curve, a pro-funnel KPI, a unit-economics shift. You're accountable for the number alongside your team. How do you scope to actually move it, decide what \*not\* to build, and have the discipline to follow up 2–4 weeks after launch?

### **What Success Looks Like (Year 1)**

* **Initiative outcomes hit** — You've shipped 3–4 initiatives end-to-end, and at least two clearly moved their metric (with the post-launch review to prove it).
* **Agent workflow that travels** — The prompts, evals, and review loop you built are picked up by peers on other initiatives.
* **Faster cycle time** — Median time from problem-framing to first production rollout on your initiatives is meaningfully shorter.
* **Quality holds** — No customer- or pro-facing regression traceable to agent-authored code that slipped through your review.
* **Visible leverage** — Peers point to artifacts you left behind — runbooks, evals, agent workflows, post-launch write-ups — as references they use.

  
**Requirements**  

### **Who You Are**

* **AI-native.** Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or equivalent are how you ship today — daily, on production work. You have real opinions about prompts, evals, agent loops, and review workflows, and you've built a workflow where agents write all of the code while you steer, review, and verify.
* **Operating at a lead level.** Whatever your current title, you've been the person making the call, shipping the hard thing, and standing behind whether it worked.
* **Outcome-driven.** You measure your week in "did the metric move" and "did the experience get better." You read the post-launch dashboard and own the answer.
* **A strong horizontal partner.** You hold your own with a strong PM and designer, and you collaborate well with engineering peers in a shared codebase. You bring engineering judgment to product calls and product judgment to engineering calls.
* **Decisive and documented.** You make architecture, data-model, and rollout calls, write them down, get fast input, and move.
* **A force multiplier.** Your impact compounds beyond your own initiative because you leave reusable artifacts behind — agent workflows, evals, runbooks, post-launch reviews.
* **Customer- and pro-minded.** This is a real marketplace with real people on both sides, and you care about the outcomes for both.

### **Good to Know**

* **An individual-contributor role with room to grow.** People management sits with the EM — but the path into management is an open door for those who want it.
* **A product-engineering role, end-to-end.** You ship features that move metrics; platform and architecture work happen inside the initiative when the outcome needs them.
* **Hands-on, with a high quality bar.** Agents handle much of the implementation; you bring the judgment, design, safety, and accountability. The bar is high.
* **Shipping to a live marketplace.** With $150M+ in bookings, customers and pros use what you ship within the same week.

### **Tech You'll Touch**

* **AI agents** — Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, internal agent stack, MCP servers, evals tooling
* **Backend** — PHP/Laravel
* **Frontend** — TypeScript/React/React Native (customer & pro apps, web and mobile)
* **Data** — Redshift, dbt, Segment, Airflow
* **Infra** — AWS, Datadog, Sentry, GitHub Actions
* **Documentation & process** — Brain (Claude Code skills + docs repo), Confluence, Jira

You don't need every box checked. You need deep skill in at least one of our stacks plus credible production experience with AI coding agents.

 **Benefits**  

* Competitive salary of USD $85,000–$125,000 annual base
* Work from anywhere
* High ownership and autonomy
* Fast-moving team that loves to build, learn, and grow

jobs.title: Product Manager (Reporting Team)
jobs.description:
At **AI Digital**, reporting is how clients see what their programmatic and performance campaigns are achieving. You’ll own every part of it: client dashboards, AI analysis features, advanced research reports and the Reporting API. The goal is to give clients more value from reporting while cutting the manual work it takes to produce it. We are looking for a **Product Manager** who understands how media performance is measured and reported, and who wants to own a whole portfolio of reporting products from start to finish.

**Responsibilities:**

* Own the backlog and roadmap for the Reporting portfolio: Native and ClicData dashboards, AI features (AI Campaign Analyst, Optimization Log, deck generation in Elevate), research reports (P2C, Brand Study, MMM) and the Reporting API.
* Lead the transition from ClicData (third-party BI tool) to in-house Native dashboards, and set the rules for when each is used.
* Drive adoption of Native dashboards and Optimization Log, with the goal of near-100% Optimization Log adoption across campaigns.
* Launch new reporting formats, such as Advanced Reach and vertical-specific reporting (healthcare, agriculture and others).
* Improve the Reporting API: add new sources and support customizations while keeping operational costs low.
* Work with AI & Automation Engineering, BI and Data Engineering on reports prepared for internal teams.
* Support Growth team requests, such as an internal version of dashboards or AI chat with permissioned access to data.
* Balance client value against operational cost in every product decision.

* 3+ years of product management experience on data, analytics or reporting products in B2B, ideally in adtech, martech or media.
* Working knowledge of BI and data visualization tools (Tableau, Looker, Power BI or similar) and dashboard design principles.
* Enough technical depth to discuss data sources, pipelines, APIs and data models with BI and Data Engineering, and to make architecture trade-offs with them.
* A track record of driving adoption of a product, not only shipping it.
* Strong communication skills with C1-level English, written and spoken.

**Nice to have:**

* Hands-on experience with simple LLM-based tools and an understanding of how AI features are built and how their output quality is evaluated.
* Familiarity with digital marketing channels, programmatic advertising and campaign performance metrics, and how they are reported to clients.
* SQL, ideally BigQuery, to check numbers and investigate data issues.
* Familiarity with measurement and research methods such as MMM, brand lift studies, attribution, and reach and frequency.
* Experience with vertical-specific data, such as healthcare.
* Ability to prototype in Figma or with AI prototyping tools.

jobs.title: Especialista de CX Intelligence
jobs.description:
**Responsabilidades e atribuições:**

Você fará parte de um time que enxerga a experiência do comprador de ponta a ponta nas frentes de Imóveis, Autos e Goods do Grupo OLX. Nossa missão é identificar as dores da jornada, quantificar o impacto delas e endereçar as oportunidades de experiência que movem os resultados do negócio. O time faz a ponte entre a voz do cliente e os indicadores de negócio, transformando insight em ação priorizada.

Nesta posição, você será ao mesmo tempo parceiro de Produto, para influenciar e co-construir soluções, e conector entre todas as áreas que tocam o cliente, garantindo que a empresa olhe para ele de forma end to end, e não por silos ou etapas isoladas.

* Acompanhar de forma recorrente NPS, Contact Rate, Churn e Recompra, por vertical (Imóveis, Autos, Goods) e por etapa da jornada.
* Construir e manter a conexão entre as métricas de experiência e os resultados de negócio, evidenciando correlações e impacto real das dores que são relatadas pelos nosso.
* Traduzir os achados em recomendações objetivas e priorizadas por impacto e esforço.
* Identificar desvios, tendências e alertas, e comunicá-los de forma clara às áreas responsáveis.
* Conduzir análises aprofundadas combinando dados quantitativos (métricas, comportamento, contatos) e qualitativos (verbatims, pesquisas, tickets, entrevistas). Identificar a causa raiz das dores, e não apenas os sintomas, e dimensionar o tamanho do problema.
* Mapear a jornada end to end do comprador, com visão de pontos de contato, processos, sistemas e áreas envolvidas.
* Construir o cenário AS IS vs TO BE, evidenciando as dores mapeadas com números concretos (volume de contatos, queda de NPS, perda de conversão, churn, impacto em recompra).
* Estruturar e conduzir rituais de governança para acompanhar o plano de ações de experiência com as áreas responsáveis.
* Atuar como parceiro direto do time de Produto, influenciando a priorização do roadmap com base em dados e na voz do cliente, e co-construindo soluções desde o discovery até o pós-lançamento.
* Participar da definição de hipóteses, requisitos e métricas de sucesso de novas funcionalidades e melhorias, junto a Design, Tecnologia, Atendimento e Negócio.
* Construção de blueprints da jornada do cliente, traduzindo a visão fragmentada de cada área em uma visão única e integrada da jornada do cliente, apontando dependências, gaps e sobreposições. Conectar os pontos entre Produto, Atendimento, Marketing, Operações, Dados e demais áreas, evidenciando como decisões em uma etapa da jornada impactam a experiência nas etapas seguintes.

**Requisitos e qualificações:**  
  

* Experiência prévia atuando como Customer Experience charpter ou PM, com foco em Voz do Cliente, Customer Insights, Product Analytics, Business Analytics ou áreas correlatas.
* Perfil de dono, com autonomia, organização e foco em execução e resultado. É fundamental que o candidato tenha perfil organizado e preze pela qualidade das análises realizadas, tanto em termos de assertividade, clareza, storytelling e apresentação.
* Domínio de métricas de experiência e negócio (NPS, Contact Rate, Churn, Recompra) e capacidade de relacioná-las entre si.
* Experiência em mapeamento de jornadas e blueprints, com habilidade de criar análises AS IS vs TO BE de forma simplificada, e quantificar oportunidades. Visão end to end e capacidade de conectar experiência do cliente a resultados de negócio.
* Forte raciocínio analítico: facilidade para trabalhar com dados, estruturar hipóteses, dimensionar impacto e construir business cases. Experiência em análises de causa raiz combinando dados quantitativos e qualitativos.
* Experiência em atuar de forma próxima a times de Produto, Operações, Marketing e Dados, influenciando decisões e co-construindo soluções.
* Conhecimento de ferramentas de mapeamento colaborativo (Miro, Figma).

**Desejáveis:**  
  

* Conhecimento de marketplaces, classificados ou e-commerce, preferencialmente nos segmentos de imóveis, veículos e bens de consumo.
* Vivência com ferramentas de análise de dados (SQL, Looker, Tableau ou similares).
* 2 anos de atuação como PM ou CX charpter.
* Vivência com casos de uso de IA aplicados a atendimento e experiência.
* Experiência em metodologias ágeis e em co-criação com times de produto.

  
**Benefícios:**  
  
Remuneração compatível com o mercado
